title: 40 per hour annual salary: How to calculate your full-time pay in Australia
description: Convert $40 per hour to annual salary using the standard 38-hour week. Includes tax, super, fortnightly pay, and comparisons with the National Minimum Wage.
salarySummary: At $40 per hour and 38 hours per week, your annual salary is $79,040 before tax and super, with a fortnightly gross of $3,040.

faqs.q: How is the annual salary calculated from $40 per hour?

If you work a different number of hours, adjust the weekly hours accordingly. This method assumes the same rate every week with no unpaid overtime or penalty rates.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the 40 per hour annual salary

If you earn $40 per hour, your annual salary depends on the number of hours you work each week. The standard full-time week in Australia is 38 hours, as defined by the Fair Work Ombudsman. Using the formula **hourly rate × hours per week × 52**, a $40 per hour annual salary works out to **$79,040** before tax and super. This is a common benchmark for many skilled roles and sits well above the [National Minimum Wage](/topics/minimum-wage) of $26.44 per hour (from 1 July 2026).

### How the calculation works

To convert $40 per hour to an annual figure, multiply by your weekly hours. For a 38-hour week:

- Annual: $40 × 38 × 52 = $79,040
- Fortnightly: $40 × 38 × 2 = $3,040 gross
- Weekly: $40 × 38 = $1,520 gross

If you work fewer or more hours, adjust the weekly figure. For example, a 40-hour week would give $40 × 40 × 52 = $83,200 per year. The formula assumes the same rate every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. For a more precise estimate, use the [timesheet](/), which lets you enter your base hourly rate and optionally add casual loading.

### Comparing $40 per hour with award rates and the minimum wage

The National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour for permanent employees. At $40 per hour, you are earning about 51% more than the minimum. However, many modern awards set higher minimum rates for specific industries and classifications. For example, a retail employee or a hospitality worker may have a different award rate. The $40 per hour figure is not a median or average for any particular job; it is simply a rate you might be offered or negotiate. If you want to see how your rate compares with industry averages, refer to the [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page, which uses ABS data (full-time adult ordinary time earnings were $2,083.70 per week in May 2026).

### Casual loading and superannuation

If you are a casual employee, you are entitled to a 25% casual loading on top of your base hourly rate. For a $40 base rate, the casual rate becomes **$50 per hour**. This loading compensates for the lack of paid leave. When using the [timesheet](/), you can check a box to add the 25% loading automatically. **Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading**; always start with the base rate.

Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings. The super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary time earnings (from 1 July 2026). For a $40 per hour annual salary of $79,040, the super contribution would be $9,485 per year, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. This means your total employment cost is $88,525. For more details on how super affects your pay, see [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

### Tax and take-home pay

Using the 2026–27 resident tax rates, the tax on $79,040 is calculated as:
- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on the next $26,800 ($4,020)
- 30% on the remaining $34,040 ($10,212)
- Total tax: $14,232 (rounded to $14,236 in the estimate)
- Medicare levy: 2% of $79,040 = $1,581 (using single reduction thresholds from 2025–26)
- After-tax income: approximately $63,223 per year, or $2,432 per fortnight.

This is an estimate. Your actual tax may differ if you have a HELP debt, Medicare levy surcharge, or salary packaging. The [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page provides more context on deductions.

### Why the 38-hour week is standard

The Fair Work Commission sets the standard full-time week at 38 hours for most awards. When you see a $40 per hour annual salary quoted, it usually assumes 38 hours unless stated otherwise. Some roles may have a 35-hour or 40-hour week, so always confirm your ordinary hours. The formula works for any weekly hours: just multiply by 52.

### Fortnightly pay and budgeting

Many employers pay fortnightly. At $40 per hour for 38 hours per week, your gross fortnightly pay is $3,040. After tax and Medicare, you would receive about $2,432 per fortnight. This can help with budgeting and comparing job offers. The [reference tables](/data) include pre-calculated figures for common hourly rates.

### Important considerations

- **Award vs. minimum wage:** Your rate may be set by an award, which could be higher than the National Minimum Wage. The $40 per hour figure is above both, but check your specific award.
- **Casual loading:** If you are casual, your total hourly pay is $50 (base $40 + 25% loading). The annual salary calculation should use the base rate for super and award comparisons.
- **Super is extra:** The $79,040 annual salary does not include super. Your employer pays super on top.
- **No overtime or penalties:** The simple formula does not account for overtime rates, penalty rates, or allowances. Your actual annual earnings may be higher if you work additional hours.
- **Estimates only:** This is a guide, not a determination of your pay or tax. Use the [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) page for other rates.

### Summary

A $40 per hour annual salary, based on a 38-hour week, is $79,040 gross. After tax and Medicare, you take home about $63,223 per year. Fortnightly, that is $3,040 gross and approximately $2,432 net. Super adds $9,485 on top. Whether you are comparing a job offer or planning your budget, understanding this conversion helps you make informed decisions about your pay.
